clue.text: Clegg initially gave undertaking to keep sacred word, but made concessions

indicators.note: to keep means the sacred word is held inside the run made by the first two pieces
initially asks for the opening letter of the name Clegg

parts.note: to give an undertaking is to have promised something
Om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist worship

explanation.surface: Nick Clegg made a solemn pledge, then backed down in coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Nick Clegg, Liberal Democrat leader, whose broken tuition-fees pledge in the 2010 coalition made his concessions topical; 'to keep' holds the sacred word just after his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has compromised has given ground and settled for less than they wanted, which is making concessions.

clue.text: Middle Eastern coverage of tea party Republican

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A US Tea Party Republican is reported on from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the American Tea Party movement, but tea and party are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A chador is the full-length cloak worn by women in Iran and nearby, a garment that covers the body.

clue.text: Sondheim's last song? Not by a long way

definitions.text: Sondheim's last song? Not by a long way

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the name Sondheim

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: Was this really Sondheim's final song? Far from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: M (the end of Sondheim) plus ARIA gives the West Side Story song, from 1957, which was nowhere near his final one.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is a love song with lyrics by Stephen Sondheim from West Side Story, written early in his career.

clue.text: ANile trip might produce creature of this sort?

definitions.text: ANile trip might produce creature of this sort?

indicators.note: might produce says the letters of the phrase can be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: A holiday on the Nile could well bring you face to face with a crocodile.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: rearrange A NILE TRIP and you get a word for the kind of creature, such as a crocodile, a Nile cruise might show you.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptilian describes animals of the crocodile and snake class, the kind of beast seen on a Nile cruise.

clue.text: Manipulation of service period

parts.note: Mass is the Eucharist service in the Catholic church
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: How long a church service takes is a matter of handling.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage is kneading and rubbing of the body, a physical manipulation of the muscles.

clue.text: "Gor Blimey" trousers with the end at the top, covering father's middle

indicators.note: covering, in a down entry, means the first part sits above the second

indicators.text: with the end at the top
indicators.note: with the end at the top means the final letter of the trousers word is brought round to the front

parts.note: trews are close-fitting tartan trousers

indicators.note: middle asks for the central pair of letters of the word father

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at a pair of trousers worn upside down over Dad's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: TREWS with its last letter moved to the front gives STREW; 'covering' places it above TH, the middle of father, in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewth is a dated British and Australian exclamation of surprise, a mild oath like gor blimey.

clue.text: Gets rid of largely unintelligent epilogue

indicators.note: largely means most of the word is used, losing its last letter

parts.note: dumb is an informal word for unintelligent
a PS, or postscript, is an addition at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone discards a rather stupid closing section.
explanation.definitionFit: To dump something is to throw it away or get shot of it.

clue.text: Flat writer's block?

explanation.surface: A writer cannot work in their own apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' is the condition of being stuck, but here it means literally a block of paper for writing on.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is informal for a home or apartment, and also a block of sheets of writing paper.

clue.text: Special benefit announced: one piece of bread each

indicators.note: announced means the word for a special benefit is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a perk is a special benefit that comes with a job
a means one
pita, also spelt pitta, is a flat Middle Eastern bread

explanation.surface: A special benefit is declared: everyone gets a slice of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: PERK said aloud gives the PER C of the answer; 'piece of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for by heads, meaning for each person.

clue.text: Let fate decide if Lord West's sacked

indicators.note: sacked, as in a city being plundered and wrecked, tells us to jumble the letters

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Leave it to chance whether a peer called Lord West is fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' turns LORD WEST (the 's adds no letter) into the answer. Lord West was a former First Sea Lord and Labour security minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw lots is to choose by chance, leaving the outcome to luck.

clue.text: Oddly absent campers on plots unlike 13

indicators.note: oddly absent means the odd-numbered letters are dropped and only the even ones kept

explanation.surface: Unlike the lighthouse clue, people camping on plots go missing in strange ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'campers on plots' as one run of letters and keep every second one. 13 is BESIDE THE POINT, meaning irrelevant, so 'unlike 13' asks for relevant.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent or to the purpose, the opposite of irrelevant.

clue.text: That's about the long and short of communication, Ruth

parts.note: re means about or concerning

parts.words: the long and short of communication
parts.note: Morse code sends messages with long and short signals, dashes and dots

explanation.surface: This is the gist of a conversation with someone called Ruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name, but here it is the old word for pity or regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is an archaic word for sorrow or pity, so it means regret for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Shot up on A1, motor's brought in with holed instrument

indicators.note: brought in means the motor word is placed inside the jumbled letters
shot up suggests something blown apart, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: A1 reads as the letter A and the figure 1 as I
a motor is an informal word for a car

explanation.surface: A man named Al is shot, and his car is pulled in by a holed instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot up' looks like a shooting, but it is the anagram signal; 'brought in' sets the car just after the first letter of the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocarina is a small egg-shaped wind instrument with finger holes.

clue.text: Welsh attack drinking tradition

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: A Welsh assault turns out to be a custom for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Wassail is the old Christmas custom of drinking healths with spiced ale.

clue.text: The lighthouse may be irrelevant

explanation.surface: The lighthouse might be beside the point.
explanation.walkthrough: Lighthouses often stand on a point, a headland, so one may literally stand next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighthouse often stands next to a headland; the phrase also means off the subject.

clue.text: Moved sneakily past nurse, getting around another, and injected with poison

indicators.note: past means the first piece goes before what follows it

parts.note: EN is a crossword abbreviation for an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: getting around means the jumbled letters enclose the second nurse
sneakily suggests something shifting slyly, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: another nurse gives a second EN

explanation.surface: Someone crept past a nurse and dodged another before being given a poisoned injection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved sneakily past' reads as one action, but Moved is the fodder for 'sneakily' and 'past' puts the first nurse in front; 'getting around' holds the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Envenomed means filled with venom, so poisoned as by a snake bite.

clue.text: Write largely tedious stuff principally about Oxford swinging

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool, and to pen is to write

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the university abbreviation
largely means most of the word is used, dropping its last letter

parts.note: dull means tedious

indicators.note: principally asks for the opening letter of stuff

parts.note: OU is short for Oxford University

explanation.surface: Someone writes long boring material mainly about swinging Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging' seems to describe Oxford, as in the swinging sixties, but it is the definition; 'about' wraps the shortened word and the S round the university.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pendulous hangs down and sways loosely, like a pendulum.

clue.text: Record energy levels with this helping make orgasm eternal

indicators.note: helping make means the answer is just part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: This device makes an orgasm last for ever and records your energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the two words: or-GASM ETER-nal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter is a device that records how much gas fuel a home uses.

clue.text: Commercial opening clear — and transformed into seasonal Windows application

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
a vent is an opening for air

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of the two words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A computer ad promotes a holiday program for Microsoft Windows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windows' suggests computer software, but this has little paper windows to open each day before Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christmas countdown calendar has small doors or flaps opened each December day.

clue.text: South American setter's inclined to support church

indicators.note: to support, in a down entry, means the later pieces sit below the first

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, and setter's stands for setter is
to lean is to be inclined

explanation.surface: The crossword setter tends to back the church in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in setter's is 'is', so it gives I and the link 'is'; 'to support' sets I + LEAN beneath CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chilean is a person from Chile, a country in South America.

clue.text: Politicians collared by Left union leaders over money making one-off payment

indicators.note: over, in a down entry, means the earlier letters sit above the next
collared by means the politicians are held inside the other letters
leaders, in the plural, takes the first letter of union twice

parts.note: the leader of union is its letter U
MPs are Members of Parliament
M stands for money, as in M1 and M2 money supply

explanation.surface: MPs are grabbed by left-wing union bosses in a row about money.
explanation.walkthrough: MPS go between LU and UM, where both Us come from union's leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made all at once, not in instalments.

clue.text: The unhinged controlled capital

indicators.note: unhinged means mad, so the letters of the little word are jumbled

parts.note: to run something is to control it, so ran means controlled

explanation.surface: A mad person was in charge of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Tehran is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: Cycling robes make for a singular way to go downhill!

definitions.text: a singular way to go downhill!

indicators.note: cycling means letters are moved round from the front of the word to the end

parts.note: kimonos are loose Japanese robes

explanation.surface: Wearing cycling gear makes for an odd way to go down a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling' moves KI from the front of KIMONOS to the end. 'singular' hints at mono-, one ski.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoski is one wide ski with both feet fixed to it, used on snow slopes.

clue.text: Male sheep coming up against male fawn

indicators.note: against means the second piece is placed right next to the first
coming up, in a down entry, means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: Some rams rise to face a male deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like a young deer, which suits the sheep in the surface, but it is the verb meaning to flatter.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarm is to flatter in an oily way, which is what fawning means.

clue.text: Loose woman's first one with 100% success rate getting men?

definitions.text: one with 100% success rate getting men?

indicators.note: first means the woman's name comes before the other piece

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the woman's name Maureen; woman's here is woman is
to loose is to untie or set free

explanation.surface: A promiscuous woman is the first who always gets her man?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose woman' looks like one phrase but splits. The definition plays on the saying that a Canadian Mountie always gets his man.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, famous for always catching the wanted man.

clue.text: Three Tenors performing with you and I in a piece for everyone

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces in a new order

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor, so three tenors give three Ts
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: The Three Tenors sing with you and me in a song for all.
explanation.walkthrough: The Three Tenors were Pavarotti, Domingo and Carreras, but here they are just three Ts; 'performing' makes TUTT before the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti, Italian for all, marks a musical passage played by every performer.

clue.text: Dish of minced lamb -in tripe, oddly

indicators.note: in means the jumbled meat goes inside the letters taken from tripe
oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of tripe
minced means chopped up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dish of minced lamb served in tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minced' is a real cooking word in the surface, yet it is the anagram signal, giving MBAL; 'oddly' and 'in' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a dish of meat or fish baked in a drum-shaped mould.

clue.text: Bike company occupying rundown store

indicators.note: occupying means the company sits inside the jumbled shop letters
rundown means dilapidated, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A bicycle firm has moved into a shabby shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rundown' reads as a shop's shabby state, and it is the anagram signal too, making SOTER; 'occupying' sets the company after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A scooter is a light motorbike with small wheels.

clue.text: Free passage most of the way

indicators.note: most of the way means the word is used nearly to its end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a ride is a passage or journey on a vehicle

explanation.surface: A free trip covering almost the whole route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free passage' looks like one phrase, but Free is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid someone of something is to deliver or set them free from it.

clue.text: Terminating restrictive contract — to keep Rooney at Old Trafford?

definitions.text: to keep Rooney at Old Trafford?

explanation.surface: Ending a binding deal would keep Rooney at Manchester United.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Trafford is Manchester United's ground; the second part reads as MAN U MISSION, the club's aim in 2010 when Wayne Rooney threatened to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Manumission is the formal freeing of a slave, ending bondage; the second reading is Man U's goal.
